questions.q: Where does the lovely road described in the opening run from?
questions.explain: The chapter opens: 'There is a lovely road that runs from Ixopo into the hills.'

questions.q: How far does the road climb into the hills to reach Carisbrooke?
questions.explain: 'The road climbs seven miles into them, to Carisbrooke.'

questions.q: From the tops, you look down on the valley of which river?
questions.explain: The view is over the valley of the Umzimkulu, on its journey from the Drakensberg to the sea.

questions.q: Which bird's 'forlorn crying' can be heard in the veld?
questions.explain: The titihoya is named as 'one of the birds of the veld'; later, in the ruined land, 'the titihoya does not cry here any more.'

questions.q: Why is the grass on the tops rich and matted, so that 'you cannot see the soil'?
choices: It is well-tended, with few cattle and few fires, and it holds the rain and mist
It has never been grazed at all
questions.explain: The kept grass holds the rain and mist, which seep in and feed the streams in every kloof.

questions.q: What does the narrator tell the reader to do on the tended grass, 'for the ground is holy'?
questions.explain: 'Stand unshod upon it, for the ground is holy, being even as it came from the Creator.'

questions.q: The refrain about the land warns: 'Keep it, guard it, care for it, for it keeps men... ' — and then?
questions.explain: The land's health and the people's survival are bound together: 'Destroy it and man is destroyed.'

questions.q: What has happened to the hills lower down, as they fall to the valley?
choices: They grow red and bare and can no longer hold the rain and mist
They have been terraced for farming
questions.explain: Below the tops the hills 'grow red and bare; they cannot hold the rain and mist, and the streams are dry in the kloofs.'

questions.q: In the valleys of the broken land, who is left to scratch at the soil?
choices: Women, old men and old women, and children
questions.explain: 'They are valleys of old men and old women, of mothers and children. The men are away, the young men and the girls are away.'

questions.q: Why, according to the chapter, are the young men and girls gone from the valley?
choices: The soil cannot keep them any more, so they have left
They are away fighting a war
They have been forcibly removed by the government
questions.explain: 'The soil cannot keep them any more' — the exhausted land drives its people away, a theme that frames the whole novel.
